starter:
# A Composition2Yaml document: the candidate chosen for each task of a workflow, and the values it yields.
# Without a problem the values are the ones you declare. Link a problem revision (problem: {ref, compilation})
# and the gateway computes and verifies them when you seal.
syntaxVersion: "1.0"
composition: my-composition
version: 1.0.0
kind: application
workflow:
  seq:
    - signIn
    - notify
binding:
  signIn: {local: true}
  notify: {candidate: email.provider.basic}
values:
  cost: {value: 10, unit: EUR/month}

sections.name: The smallest document
sections.description: Seven keys are required: `syntaxVersion` (the language version, quoted), `composition` (the slug), `version` (the document's own label, semver), `kind`, `workflow`, `binding` and `values`. Here one task is bound to one candidate, and nothing is measured yet.
sections.yaml:
syntaxVersion: "1.0"
composition: hello
version: 0.1.0
kind: workflow
workflow: greet
binding: {greet: {candidate: greeter}}
values: {}

sections.name: Workflow forms
sections.description: A task id is a step. `seq` runs its steps in order, `and` runs them in parallel, `xor` takes exactly one branch (with probabilities that add up to exactly 1, or `uniform: true`), and `loop` repeats a step `count` times, or `expected` times on average. `null` is the empty step.

sections.name: Binding and provenance
sections.description: Every task of the workflow has exactly one entry: a `candidate` of the problem (its id, or `<resource>/<id>` when two catalogs share the id), or `local: true` for work done in house. `from` says which plan of a SPHERE pricing the candidate came from, at a pinned pricing `version`; `registry` names an on-premise SPHERE this installation defines.

sections.name: Values and units
sections.description: `values` are the global values the binding yields. A bare number is dimensionless (an availability, a count); `{value, unit}` carries its unit exactly as written. Without a problem the values are declared; with one, a seal computes and verifies them.

sections.name: Linked to a problem
sections.description: `problem` names the BIM problem revision the composition was chosen in, and the compilation it is evaluated against. A seal then checks the binding against the problem and computes the values.

sections.name: An offering in SPHERE
sections.description: `offering` is optional: the composition's own pricing, by reference only. Its plans, prices and limits stay in SPHERE. `{sphere: <owner/name>}` is a pricing of this installation's SPHERE; `{sphere, registry}` is one on an on-premise SPHERE.

sections.name: An offering as a Pricing2Yaml file
sections.description: The third source: `{url: https://…}`, a public Pricing2Yaml file over HTTPS, with no credentials. An offering has exactly one source and no version.

sections.name: A syntax version written as a number
sections.description: YAML reads an unquoted `1.0` as a number, so `syntaxVersion` must be quoted.
sections.yaml:
syntaxVersion: 1.0
composition: hello
version: 0.1.0
kind: workflow
workflow: greet
binding: {greet: {candidate: greeter}}
values: {}

sections.name: Constraints belong to the problem
sections.description: Alternatives, constraints, objectives, demand and its variants are the BIM problem's; weights belong to a run preset. A document that writes them is refused.
sections.yaml:
syntaxVersion: "1.0"
composition: shop
version: 1.0.0
kind: application
workflow: pick
binding: {pick: {candidate: c_pick}}
values: {}
constraints: [{max: {latency: 100}}]

sections.name: Presentation stays in the renderer
sections.description: How a composition is drawn (sections, highlights, labels) is decided by the screen that renders it, never by the document: `presentation` is an unknown key.
